title: Canadian adult skills and learning characteristics
description: Survey-weighted marginal distributions derived from 11,697 Canadian respondents in PIAAC Cycle 2.

reference_population.label: Adults aged 16-65 represented by the Canadian PIAAC Cycle 2 public-use file

methodology.sampling_assumption: Using these dimensions independently produces synthetic combinations and does not preserve respondent-level relationships. Sampling respondent records is preferred when those relationships matter.
methodology.skill_estimation: Skill-level shares average estimates across all 10 plausible values for each cognitive domain.
methodology.caution: Self-assessed performance is a confidence-related proxy, not a direct measure of general confidence, AI confidence, or AI literacy.

literacy_proficiency.description: Ability to access, understand, evaluate, and use written texts.

numeracy_proficiency.description: Ability to access, use, and reason with mathematical information.

adaptive_problem_solving_proficiency.description: Ability to solve problems in changing and dynamic situations.

self_assessed_performance.description: Respondents' estimate of the percentage of assessment questions they answered correctly; used only as a confidence-related proxy.

ict_use_at_home.description: Ordered index of ICT-skill use at home among respondents with valid data.

ict_use_at_work.description: Ordered index of ICT-skill use at work among respondents on an applicable work pathway.

curiosity.description: Cycle 2 curiosity-facet score grouped relative to its Canadian weighted standard-score distribution.

learning_at_work.description: Ordered index of learning practices at work among respondents on an applicable work pathway.

recent_nonformal_education.description: Participation in non-formal education during the previous 12 months among respondents with valid data.
